parties.host: Whoever runs OpenClear: the bank when it hosts OpenClear itself, or its hosting provider

evidence.automated: OpenClear's own data shows whether it operates; a test can attest to it for a period
evidence.assisted: OpenClear supplies the evidence (a report, an export, a recorded review); a person judges it
evidence.attested: outside what OpenClear can see; a person attests, and may attach evidence

planned_checks.access_review: A bank-wide access review recorded within the last quarter, every membership in it confirmed or changed
planned_checks.change_impact_replay: Every rule or model change approved in the period had a replay run against it beforehand
planned_checks.control_response: How long each control spent at WARN or FAIL in the period before it returned to PASS
planned_checks.customer_access_review: Each self-managing customer recorded an access review of its people within the last quarter
planned_checks.customer_api_client_secrets: A customer's API clients: secrets rotated within a year, or key pairs
planned_checks.customer_decision_timeliness: A customer's exceptions decided before their deadline over the period
planned_checks.customer_dormant_users: A customer's people who haven't signed in for 90 days, and leavers still active
planned_checks.customer_mfa: The share of customer people who sign in with a second factor or the customer's identity provider
planned_checks.customer_sod: Customer people who can both submit issued items and decide exceptions
planned_checks.customer_sso: A customer-managed identity provider in use, and when SCIM last changed anyone
planned_checks.decision_delivery: Every decision file delivered to the core before its cutoff, and acknowledged
planned_checks.default_dispositions: Every account with positive pay has a default disposition for undecided exceptions
planned_checks.dormant_accounts: Staff who haven't signed in for 90 days, and deactivations later than the bank's deadline
planned_checks.dual_control: Dual control on, and every decision in the period made by a different person from its recommender
planned_checks.evidence_export: An evidence export taken within the last quarter
planned_checks.file_reconciliation: Each presented-items file's item count and total, matched against the control totals the core sent
planned_checks.integration_tls: Every webhook and delivery destination uses HTTPS
planned_checks.key_age: The signing and field-encryption keys' ages against the host's rotation period
planned_checks.model_pooling_acknowledged: Someone with authority acknowledged the shared-model pooling disclosure
planned_checks.outside_services: The outside services turned on (email, SMS, OCR, storage, identity providers), with when each was reviewed
planned_checks.password_policy: The bank's password policy against the minimum the bank records as its standard
planned_checks.platform_staff: The platform's staff, each with a second factor, and their support access in the period
planned_checks.privileged_accounts: How many people hold admin permissions, and any who haven't signed in for 90 days
planned_checks.rejected_rows: Upload rows rejected and not corrected or resubmitted within a business day
planned_checks.scheduled_jobs: Each scheduled job's last run, against its schedule
planned_checks.scim_sync: When SCIM or the identity provider last changed anyone, and staff the directory has disabled who are still active
planned_checks.software_currency: The running version's age, and releases since it
planned_checks.stale_ach_authorizations: ACH authorizations unused for a year, or past their end date and not revoked
planned_checks.staff_mfa: Everyone who can decide exceptions or change data signs in with a second factor or the bank's identity provider
planned_checks.support_access_review: Support access grants in the period: each named, with a reason and an end, none open-ended
planned_checks.transport_security: Requests arrive over HTTPS, with HSTS set
planned_checks.two_person_changes: Every rule or model change in the period approved by a second admin
planned_checks.wsud_signed: Every ACH debit returned as unauthorized has a signed Written Statement of Unauthorized Debit

cuecs.title: Provision and remove staff
cuecs.statement: Approve each staff member's access before adding them, change it when their job changes, and deactivate them in OpenClear (or in the bank's identity provider) by the bank's own deadline when they leave.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear grants only what a person's security group allows, records every membership change in the action log, and stops a deactivated person signing in or using a token at once.
cuecs.where: Users → Export (with last sign-in); user.* and membership.* in the action log

cuecs.title: Keep the identity provider in step
cuecs.statement: When staff sign on through the bank's identity provider, keep its group mapping and SCIM provisioning in step with the bank's directory, so someone disabled there is disabled in OpenClear.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear applies SCIM deactivations and group changes as they arrive, and refuses a sign-on the identity provider refuses.
cuecs.where: Settings → Sign-on; scim.* in the action log

cuecs.title: Review staff access
cuecs.statement: At least quarterly, review each staff member's security group, customer scope and account access, remove what's no longer needed, and record the review.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear exports every membership with its group, scope, account access and last sign-in, and records each change.
cuecs.where: Users → Export; the access review record (CT3)

cuecs.title: Give the least access a job needs
cuecs.statement: Decide who holds admin permissions and keep them few; use customer scope and per-account access where a role is narrower than the whole bank; don't give day-to-day deciders admin permissions.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear checks every request against the person's permissions, scope and account access.

cuecs.title: Separate conflicting duties
cuecs.statement: Design security groups so no group combines conflicting duties, then move segregation of duties from warn to enforce.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear checks groups against the bank's conflict rules, refuses a breach under enforce (ERR_SOD_VIOLATION) and logs it under either mode, and never lets whoever presented an item decide it.
cuecs.where: Settings → Segregation of duties; Controls; sod.violation in the action log

cuecs.title: Use dual control on decisions
cuecs.statement: Turn on dual control for pay/return decisions where the bank's policy needs a second person, and staff it so a checker is available before every cutoff.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear holds a recommended decision until a different person approves it, and records both.
cuecs.where: Settings → Decisions; decision histories in the evidence export

cuecs.title: Approve rule and model changes
cuecs.statement: Have a second admin approve every change to matching rules and scoring models, and approve only changes the bank has assessed.
cuecs.complements: Under enforce, OpenClear holds a rule or model change until another admin approves it, and records both people.
cuecs.where: Settings → Changes; the evidence export's changes

cuecs.title: Replay before changing rules
cuecs.statement: Before approving a matching-rule or model change, replay recent presented-item files through it at Model risk and review the variance report.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear's replay runs the real matching code in a dry run that's rolled back, and keeps the report.
cuecs.where: Settings → Model risk; control runs in the evidence export

cuecs.title: Second factor for admins
cuecs.statement: Make everyone who can change who may do what sign in with a security key or passkey, or only through the bank's identity provider with a second factor there.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear supports FIDO2 security keys and passkeys, and SSO-only sign-in per bank, and reports admins without either.
cuecs.where: Controls → Admins use a second factor

cuecs.title: Second factor for staff
cuecs.statement: Require a second factor (a security key or passkey, or the bank's identity provider) of everyone who can decide exceptions or change data.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear supports FIDO2 security keys and passkeys, and SSO-only sign-in per bank.

cuecs.title: Set the password policy
cuecs.statement: When password sign-in is on, set the password policy (length, character rules, lockout) to the bank's own standard.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear enforces the bank's password policy and locks an account after repeated failures.
cuecs.where: Settings → Password policy; tenant.* in the action log

cuecs.title: Look after integration credentials
cuecs.statement: Rotate API client secrets at least yearly (or use key pairs), keep them in the bank's secret store, and revoke a client when its system is retired.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear shows each secret only once, stores only its hash, supports private_key_jwt, and reports secrets over a year old.
cuecs.where: Settings → API clients; Controls → Integration secrets rotated

cuecs.title: Grant support access with care
cuecs.statement: Grant the platform's support staff access only for a stated reason and period, approve write access only when it's needed, and review each grant.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear gives support staff no access to a bank except what the bank grants, under their own name, ending on time.
cuecs.where: Settings → Support access; support_access.* in the action log

cuecs.title: Verify customers' administrators
cuecs.statement: Verify who a business customer's administrators are, and their authority to act for the customer, before giving them access or letting the customer manage its own people.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear gives a customer's people access only through the bank, or through administrators the bank has set up.
cuecs.where: Customers → People; customer.* in the action log

cuecs.title: Let customers manage themselves with care
cuecs.statement: Let a customer manage its own people or sign-on only after verifying its administrators, and make sure each customer that manages its own people has one.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear limits a self-managing customer to its own people, accounts and the roles the bank offers.

cuecs.title: Set how customers sign in
cuecs.statement: Decide how each business customer's people must sign in (password policy, second factor, the customer's own identity provider) and set it.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear enforces each customer's password policy, second factors and sign-on connection.

cuecs.title: Assess positive pay risk
cuecs.statement: Include OpenClear in the bank's risk assessment, and set each customer's services and default dispositions from it.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear applies each customer's services and default dispositions as set.

cuecs.title: Act on control status
cuecs.statement: Watch control status (the Controls page, the API, or control.status.changed in the SIEM) and investigate a WARN or FAIL by the bank's own deadline.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear tests its controls hourly and raises a security event when one changes.

cuecs.title: Run the anomaly-capture test
cuecs.statement: Turn on the daily anomaly-capture test, and investigate any synthetic fraud it misses.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear's anomaly-capture test runs injected fraud through the bank's live rules in a dry run and records what was caught.
cuecs.where: Settings → Model risk; Controls → Synthetic fraud caught

cuecs.nist_title: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
cuecs.title: Review security events and the action log
cuecs.statement: Send OpenClear's security events to the bank's SIEM (or read them through the API), alert on the ones that matter to the bank, and review the action log for unusual activity.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear records every state-changing action in a signed, hash-chained log, and delivers security events in order and at least once.
cuecs.where: Settings → Security event forwarding; Controls → Security events delivered

cuecs.title: Keep the evidence
cuecs.statement: Take an evidence export at least quarterly and keep it, with the action log's archives, for as long as the bank's retention schedule requires, in storage the bank controls.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear's evidence export is signed, so it can be checked years later without OpenClear.

cuecs.title: Decide every exception in time
cuecs.statement: Staff the exception queue so every exception is decided, by the customer or the bank, before its deadline.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear raises exceptions with their deadline, reminds before the cutoff, and applies the default disposition to anything left undecided.
cuecs.where: Controls → Decisions and imports on time

cuecs.title: Connect the core
cuecs.statement: Agree and document the interface with the core system (presented items in, decisions out), and confirm decisions are applied in the core before its cutoff.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear delivers decisions through the decision outbox, retries, and reports a late or failing delivery.
cuecs.where: Settings → Decision delivery; Controls → Decisions and imports on time

cuecs.title: Reconcile presented items
cuecs.statement: Reconcile each presented-items file OpenClear loads (its item count and total) against what the core sent, and investigate a difference.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear stores each file with its SHA-256 and a signature, and reports the items and total it loaded.

cuecs.title: Plan for an outage at the cutoff
cuecs.statement: Include positive pay in the bank's business continuity plan: what happens to exceptions and decisions if OpenClear or the core is unavailable at the cutoff, and who decides by hand.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear applies each account's default disposition to undecided exceptions, and keeps the decisions to send once the core is back.

cuecs.title: Train the deciders
cuecs.statement: Train staff who decide exceptions (fraud red flags, return deadlines and reasons, when to call the customer) before they get access, and each year.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear shows the information a decision needs, but can't judge whether the person deciding has been trained.

cuecs.title: Handle incidents involving OpenClear
cuecs.statement: Include OpenClear in the bank's incident response plan, keep the bank's incident contacts current with whoever hosts it, and report incidents involving it as the bank's rules require.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear's action log, security events and evidence export reconstruct who did what, and when.

cuecs.title: Assess the outside services turned on
cuecs.statement: Assess each outside service the bank turns on (email and SMS providers, cloud OCR, object storage, identity providers, a hosting provider) as a third party, and review it each year.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear turns no outside service on by itself, and shows which ones are on.

cuecs.title: Decide on model data pooling
cuecs.statement: Decide whether the bank's labelled decisions are pooled into the shared scoring model, and have someone with the authority to do so acknowledge the disclosure.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear pools nothing until the disclosure is acknowledged, records who acknowledged it, and offers a bank-only model.

cuecs.title: Secure the bank's integrations
cuecs.statement: Point webhooks and decision delivery at HTTPS endpoints on the bank's systems, and check each webhook's signature before acting on it.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear signs every webhook, and delivers only to a public HTTPS address.

cuecs.title: Manage the customer's own people
cuecs.statement: When the customer manages its own people, add only people it has approved, change their role when their job changes, and deactivate them the day they leave.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear keeps a customer's people to its own accounts and to the roles the bank offers, and records every change.

cuecs.title: Tell the bank about joiners and leavers
cuecs.statement: When the bank manages the customer's people, tell the bank promptly when someone joins, changes role or leaves.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear removes a person's access as soon as the bank deactivates them.

cuecs.title: Run the customer's identity provider
cuecs.statement: When the customer's people sign on through its own identity provider, require a second factor there and disable leavers there.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear accepts only the customer's verified email domains from its identity provider, and applies SCIM changes as they arrive.

cuecs.title: Review the customer's access
cuecs.statement: At least quarterly, review who in the customer can see and decide its items, and remove what's no longer needed.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear lists the customer's people with their role, accounts and last sign-in.

cuecs.title: Separate issuing from deciding
cuecs.statement: Where the customer's size allows, keep apart the people who issue checks or upload issue files and the people who decide exceptions.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear never lets the person who submitted an item decide its exception.

cuecs.title: Protect sign-in
cuecs.statement: Sign in with a security key or passkey, or through the customer's identity provider, and never share credentials.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear supports FIDO2 security keys and passkeys, and the customer's own identity provider.

cuecs.title: Look after the customer's API credentials
cuecs.statement: Rotate the customer's API client secrets (or use key pairs), keep them out of source code and shared drives, and revoke a client when its system is retired.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear shows each secret only once, stores only its hash, and supports key pairs.

cuecs.title: Send every issued check
cuecs.statement: Send OpenClear every check the customer issues, and every void, before the check can be presented, complete and accurate (serial, amount, date, and payee where the bank matches payees).
cuecs.complements: OpenClear matches presented items against what the customer sent, and raises an exception for anything that differs.

cuecs.title: Correct rejected rows
cuecs.statement: Review each upload's result and correct or resubmit any rejected rows the same business day.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear validates every row, rejects what it can't match on, and says why.

cuecs.title: Decide exceptions every day
cuecs.statement: Review exceptions every business day, decide each before its deadline, and return anything not recognized.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear raises exceptions with their deadline, reminds before the cutoff, and applies the default disposition otherwise.

cuecs.title: Keep ACH authorizations current
cuecs.statement: Keep the ACH debit authorizations (who may debit each account, and up to how much) current, and revoke one when the relationship ends.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear raises an exception for an ACH debit no authorization covers.

cuecs.title: Report fraud at once
cuecs.statement: Report suspected fraud or an unauthorized debit to the bank at once, and sign the Written Statement of Unauthorized Debit when returning an ACH debit as unauthorized.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear collects and keeps the signed statement with the return.

cuecs.title: Protect what's downloaded
cuecs.statement: Treat reports, exports and check images downloaded from OpenClear as confidential: store them encrypted, share them only with those who need them, and delete them when no longer needed.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear limits downloads to the customer's own accounts and records each export.

cuecs.title: Train against fraud and social engineering
cuecs.statement: Train the people who issue checks and decide exceptions on check fraud and social engineering, such as fake requests to change payment details or to pay an item.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear shows the information a decision needs, but can't judge whether the person deciding has been trained.

cuecs.title: Test integration changes
cuecs.statement: Test changes to the customer's own integration (issue-file exports, API clients) in the sandbox before using them in production.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear's sandbox runs the same API and file formats as production.

cuecs.title: Encrypt storage at rest
cuecs.statement: Encrypt the database, file storage (check images, uploads, archives) and backups at rest, and record how in OPENCLEAR_STORAGE_ENCRYPTION_ATTESTATION.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear encrypts stored secrets itself (AES-256-GCM) and shows the host's statement on the Controls page.

cuecs.title: Manage the keys
cuecs.statement: Generate the signing keys and the field-encryption key outside the image, keep them in a secret store, restrict who can read them, and rotate them on the host's schedule.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear refuses to start in production with development keys, versions its encryption key and re-encrypts on rotation.

cuecs.title: Serve only over HTTPS
cuecs.statement: Terminate HTTPS with a current certificate and modern TLS in front of OpenClear, and never serve it over plain HTTP.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear sets secure, SameSite cookies and a strict Content Security Policy.

cuecs.title: Lock down the origin
cuecs.statement: Let only the edge network reach OpenClear, keep the database and storage off the internet, and record how the origin is locked down.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear checks edge headers come from trusted ranges, and accepts an edge secret.

cuecs.title: Run with production settings
cuecs.statement: Run production with production settings: real keys, no development defaults, and the scheduled control tests on.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear checks its own settings at startup and on the Controls page.

cuecs.title: Back up and test restores
cuecs.statement: Back up the database and file storage, encrypted and kept apart from the primary, and test a restore at least yearly.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear's database migrations upgrade and downgrade, and its action log verifies after a restore.

cuecs.title: Apply updates
cuecs.statement: Apply OpenClear releases, and operating system, database and dependency patches, within the host's patching deadlines.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear publishes versioned releases with a changelog, and shows the running version.

cuecs.title: Scan for vulnerabilities
cuecs.statement: Scan the servers, container images and database for vulnerabilities, and fix what's found within the host's deadlines.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear's source and dependencies are public for anyone to scan.

cuecs.title: Limit administrative access to the host
cuecs.statement: Limit access to the servers, database and secret store to named administrators using a second factor, and log it. Platform staff reach a bank's data only through the bank's support access grants.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear gives platform staff no way into a bank except a grant the bank makes.
cuecs.where: Support access; the host's access records

cuecs.nist_title: Store on Separate Physical Systems or Components
cuecs.title: Keep logs off the host
cuecs.statement: Send the installation's security events and logs to a system the application's administrators can't change, and keep action-log archives in write-once storage.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear signs and chains the action log, and delivers security events to the installation's destination.

cuecs.title: Watch that it's running
cuecs.statement: Monitor /health, the job queue and the scheduled jobs, and alert someone when they stop.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear reports its health and each scheduled job's last run.

cuecs.title: Notify banks of incidents
cuecs.statement: Notify each affected bank of an incident as soon as possible, as the computer-security incident notification rule for bank service providers requires, and keep each bank's contacts current.
cuecs.complements: OpenClear's action log and security events show what happened in each bank.
